# Design the UI before the plan

The command is [`$crav1-design-ui`](reference/skills/crav1-design-ui.md). It runs after `spec.md` is accepted and before [`$crav1-plan-from-spec`](from-spec-to-plan.md).

A named person's yes on each screen is recorded with [`$crav1-record-approval`](from-record-approval.md).

**The written Markdown is the source of truth.** When a picture, a Salt block, a Mermaid block, or the HTML mock disagrees with the text, the text wins.

## First prompt

```text
$crav1-design-ui orders-dashboard

The orders dashboard screen is in the spec. Design its screens before the plan. Do not write code.
```

Add `with-mock` to also get a throwaway clickable HTML mock, or `skip-mock` to keep the visual inside the Markdown.

## Steps

| Step | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Does it apply | Answer one card only when unclear | Skips a slice with no UI, or writes `UI: none (<reason>)` on skip |
| Screens | Name the screens, or accept the list | Each `### <name> (S<n>)` with empty, loading, error and full-of-data states, interactions (click, keyboard, zoom, pan, resize, dock), and checks `(S1-C1)` |
| Look | Say the feel | The look, a layout per screen, and the tokens in one `yaml` block |
| Visual | Confirm, change, or add a type | HTML mock for zoom, docking, motion or a clickable flow; Salt for a static layout; Mermaid for flows |
| Feedback | Text, or a screenshot | Writes what a screenshot shows as text; never stores it |
| Sign-off items | One yes for all writes | Per screen: new item, material change clears the yes, typo keeps it |

## What gets written

In `docs/specs/<slug>/ui/`:

- `design.md`, the visual file: look, layout per screen, colours, fonts, and the tokens. There is no separate tokens file.
- `experience.md`, the behaviour file: the screens table, and per screen its states, interactions, flow and checks.
- `mock/index.html` only with `with-mock` or when the mock is the chosen visual. It is throwaway, never shipped, and not a plan input.

In `spec.md`, one item per screen under `## Approval needed`:

```text
- UI screen Orders list (S1): the product owner approves its layout, states and interactions in ui/design.md and ui/experience.md.
  - Person: the product owner
  - Holds: none (UI screen S1; the plan waits for this yes)
  - Screen: S1, version 3f0c9a1b2d4e, shape name=1a2b3c path=4d5e6f layout=7a8b9c states=0d1e2f interactions=3a4b5c checks=6d7e8f other=9a0b1c
```

The `Screen:` line is written by the script and never by hand. The design step never writes `Approved:`. No image, PDF or other binary file is written under `docs/specs/`.

## Sign-off, one screen at a time

- **A new screen** gets its own item; signed-off screens stay signed off.
- **A material change** (layout, states, interactions, checks, name, or path) clears that screen's yes with `Cleared: 2026-11-28, material change: the states changed`. The old `Approved:` line stays and no longer counts.
- **A typo or a non-UI edit** keeps the yes. The kit says which kind it found and why. `$crav1-add-to-spec` and the walk warn when a change touches a signed-off screen.

## What the plan and the build do with it

Each UI check becomes a task such as `- [ ] T3: Empty orders list (verify: ui — no orders shows "No orders yet") (spec: ui/experience.md S1-C1)`.

## After

Run next, with the label `Record each screen's yes, since the screens are written and wait for sign-off:` above `$crav1-record-approval`. Once a screen has its yes, `$crav1-plan-from-spec` plans it. When files changed and are not committed: `Uncommitted: 3 files; commit with $crav1-finalize-commit when ready.`
